title: Resume a killed worker on another host

authority.issuer: existing issue owner FLOW; this packet grants nothing
permitted_effects: shared_infra (authoring only; no execution from this packet)

ownership.successor_policy: Durable reassign via existing FLOW; no founder re-prompt

outcome.problem_statement: After the cloud migration a worker session can die (context exhaustion, host loss) and its mission is not durably resumable by a successor on another host.
outcome.desired_outcome: A killed worker's mission is resumed by a successor on another host from a durable checkpoint and fenced lease, with no founder re-prompt.
outcome.why_now: P0 continuity mission; session death is routine after the migration and the founder must not be the recovery procedure.
acceptance_criteria: a killed worker is resumed by a successor on another host
a stale writer is refused by the fence
the successor leaves an independent receipt of the resumed outcome
target_metrics: successor resumes the mission without a founder prompt
stale write refused with a typed failure
independent receipt names the observed outcome
explicit_non_goals: claiming production yield from a structural draft

interfaces_and_contracts: GitHub issue as canonical mission owner
alternatives_considered: a new mission ledger (rejected: duplicate layer)

deterministic_preflight: confirm the issue is open and owned
confirm the checkpoint store is reachable
confirm no competing claim on the same paths
sequencing_and_dependencies: checkpoint -> lease -> successor resume -> independent readback
external_effects: writes to the existing checkpoint store
execution.idempotency_and_reconciliation: resume is idempotent; a stale fence is refused, not merged
execution.rollback_or_compensation: drop the successor lease; the original checkpoint remains

required_tests: kill a worker mid-mission and resume on another host
no founder prompt appears in the recovery path
negative_tests: Destroy access to the primary host and prove recovery from off-host artifact.
Restore an intentionally stale checkpoint and reject conflicting writes.

profile.intent: Restore authoritative state and service after loss of a primary failure domain.
questions_to_resolve: What is the real RTO/RPO and most damaging credible common-mode failure?
Which off-host backup, signing key and restore identity are available?
How do corruption, stale snapshots, partial effects and authority revocation reconcile?
Which cold-start drill measures time to safe user path?
